newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-RESURGENT MEDVEDEV WARNS HIS RIVALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RESURGENT MEDVEDEV WARNS HIS RIVALS.

text.p: Ukrainian hitman Andrei Medvedev handed the top seeds at the Australian Open a warning on Friday after blowing away his third-round opponent.

Medvedev, who rose to a career-high world ranking of four before slipping to 36 this year, offered a sharp reminder of former achievements by demolishing Dutchman Dennis van Scheppingen 6-1 6-1 6-1 in 70 minutes.
After beating 15th seed and former Wimbledon champion Michael Stich in the second round, the Ukrainian said he would not surrender without a fight at Melbourne Park.

"Every time I step on the court -- it doesn't matter who is on the other side -- they should know they will not have an easy match. They should know they will have to struggle, that they will have to bleed," he said.

The 22-year-old from Kiev, who suffered a succession of injuries in 1996, said he was ready to challenge the world's top players again, starting with a fourth-round clash against either second seed Michael Chang or in-form Briton Tim Henman.
"I am certainly playing better than I did last year," Medvedev said. "I feel much, much stronger physically and mentally and I think I am capable of beating the top guys.
"I cannot say that I will beat them every time but I feel I have enough power and enough confidence to do it. My fitness and technical side are also good," said Medvedev.

Medvedev reached number four in the rankings in May 1994 before breaking his wrist in a quarter-final loss to Chang at the Australian Open the following year in what had been his best performance in a grand slam.
A succession of niggling back and shoulder injuries disrupted his season last year, sending his career into a nosedive from which he appears to be gradually recovering.
Medvedev has teamed up with Australian coach Bob Brett, who previously guided Boris Becker and Goran Ivanisevic, and said the victory over Stich on Wednesday provided a major boost.
"The win was the greatest feeling that I had in the last two years. It gave me a lot of confidence and just shows once again that we are on the right way," he said.
